topics.title: Ukraine announces major Patriot missile deal
topics.summary: Ukraine’s president welcomed a US-backed $2.1bn Patriot missile arrangement, while cautioning that delivery of the missiles could take years. The deal highlights the long planning horizon behind air-defence support.
topics.discussionPrompt: When something important may take years to arrive, what helps people stay patient: steady updates, small milestones, a clear plan, community support, or a totally different approach?

topics.title: G20 meeting skips its traditional group photo
topics.summary: The US cancelled a planned G20 foreign-ministers group photo after several countries declined to appear alongside Russia. The unusual diplomatic moment shows how ceremony can become part of a broader political message.
topics.discussionPrompt: Do symbolic gestures matter much in public life, or do they mostly make headlines? What ordinary group-photo rule would make gatherings less awkward?

topics.title: Russian independent newspaper announces closure
topics.summary: Novaya Gazeta, one of Russia’s best-known independent news outlets, says it will permanently close next month, citing intensifying pressure. The announcement has renewed attention on the challenges facing independent journalism.
topics.discussionPrompt: What makes you trust a news source: careful corrections, local reporting, transparent funding, expertise, seeing several viewpoints, or something else?

topics.title: Jamaican beach-access campaign gains court support
topics.summary: A temporary injunction limiting restrictions at Little Dunn’s River has encouraged campaigners seeking public access to Jamaican beaches. The case has brought fresh focus to how tourism development and shared coastal space can coexist.
topics.discussionPrompt: What local place feels like it should stay open to everyone: a beach, park, trail, library, waterfront, or town square? What makes it special?

topics.title: Biodiversity summit calls for stronger follow-through
topics.summary: COP17 biodiversity talks closed with countries reaffirming goals to protect nature and increase funding, while critics said delivery remains far behind promises. The debate centered on turning global commitments into practical action.
topics.discussionPrompt: If your neighbourhood got one realistic nature project, what would you pick: native plants, safer crossings for wildlife, cleaner streams, shade trees, community gardens, or something else?

topics.title: Experimental farm reports a boost for birds
topics.summary: A UK research farm says decades of testing wildlife-friendly practices have helped it resist broader declines in farmland birds. Its work combines food production with habitat features such as seed-rich areas and hedgerows.
topics.discussionPrompt: Could you imagine a farm as a place for both food and wildlife? Which feature sounds nicest: hedgerows, wildflower strips, ponds, nesting spaces, or something unexpected?

topics.title: South Dakota mine becomes a neutrino laboratory
topics.summary: Scientists are preparing giant underground detectors in a former South Dakota gold mine for the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment. The project aims to study elusive particles and explore basic questions about the universe.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you could ask a giant underground science experiment one question, would it be about black holes, the beginning of time, alien life, tiny particles, or something wonderfully weird?

topics.title: Chatbots become dating sidekicks for some singles
topics.summary: A survey reported that many British singles have used AI for dating advice, message drafts or confidence boosts. The trend is prompting conversations about authenticity, convenience and how people meet online.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would you ever ask an AI to help write a tricky message, or does that make it feel less like you? What kind of advice is okay to outsource?

topics.title: Tech sell-off raises questions about AI spending
topics.summary: US markets fell sharply after disappointing results at some large technology companies sharpened investor concerns about the cost and returns of AI investment. The move renewed debate over how quickly new technology can pay off.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a new invention costs a fortune before it becomes useful, what would convince you it is worth it: a practical benefit, a bold demo, lower prices, trusted experts, or patience?

topics.title: Wildlife trade may involve far more species than thought
topics.summary: A new report says the global wildlife trade involves more than twice as many plant and animal species as earlier estimates. Researchers point to trade across food, timber, fashion, ornaments and live animals.
topics.discussionPrompt: Which everyday product makes you wonder most about where it came from: seafood, wood furniture, houseplants, fashion, pets, or something else?
